rows.themePrerequisiteSkills:
1. Python & deep learning – model training with PyTorch; understanding of multi task learning (detection + segmentation).

2. Multimodal fusion – handling RGB, depth, NIR inputs; early/late fusion or attention mechanisms.

3. Object detection & segmentation – familiarity with YOLO, mask heads, mAP, mIoU evaluation.

4. Model deployment on NPU – ONNX export, INT8 quantization, ATC toolchain (ONNX→OM), Hi3403 SDK.

5. Embedded Linux & C++ (optional) – for multi sensor data synchronization and high performance inference pipeline.

rows.themeProjectDescription:
Background:

Tomato harvesting robots face illumination variations (natural, artificial, weak, sodium light) that degrade RGB image quality. Depth and near infrared (NIR) provide complementary features. A new dataset contains 4,000 triple modal samples with detection and segmentation annotations for three maturity classes (unripe, semi ripe, ripe) under four lighting conditions (10.4 GB). The Hi3403 edge NPU (10.4 TOPS) enables multi sensor fusion for real time field deployment.

Tasks (two students):

1. Student A: Design and train a lightweight fusion model (e.g., YOLOv8 seg) using RGB, depth, NIR for joint detection and segmentation.

2. Student B: Convert model (ONNX→OM), apply INT8 quantization, deploy on Hi3403, and integrate multi sensor preprocessing and inference pipeline.

Expected targets:

1. Detection mAP@0.5 ≥85%, segmentation mIoU ≥75% on test set.

2. End to end latency ≤120 ms per frame (three modalities).

3. Memory footprint ≤350 MB (INT8).

4. Robustness across ≥3 lighting conditions.

5. Deliver thesis, source code, and test report.
rows.themeTitle: Multimodal (RGB Depth NIR) Tomato Fruit Maturity Detection and Segmentation on Hi3403 NPU
rows.themeUniversity: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

rows.themeProjectDescription:
Background:

Nighttime aerial vehicle detection faces low illumination, light interference, and arbitrary orientations. The DroneVehicle Night dataset provides paired RGB IR images with oriented bounding box (OBB) annotations for five vehicle types. The Hi3403 NPU (up to 10.4 TOPS) enables edge based real time processing.

Tasks (two students):

1. Student A: Design and train a lightweight OBB detector (e.g., YOLOv8 OBB) with RGB IR fusion (early or feature level).

2. Student B: Convert model (ONNX→OM), apply INT8 quantization, deploy on Hi3403, and implement inference (NPU) + post processing (CPU).

Expected targets:

1. Detect 5 classes (car, truck, bus, van, freight).

2. mAP (OBB) ≥70% on validation set.

3. Inference latency ≤100 ms per frame on Hi3403.

4. Memory footprint ≤500 MB (INT8).

5. Deliver thesis, code (training, conversion, deployment), and test report.
rows.themeTitle: Dual Modal (RGB IR) Oriented Vehicle Detection on Hi3403 for Nighttime Drone Surveillance

rows.themeProjectDescription:
Background:

The Hi3403 edge SoC provides up to 10.4 TOPS NPU, enabling fully offline voice interaction and multimodal recognition. This eliminates cloud dependency, reduces latency, and preserves privacy for applications like assisted driving, sentry mode, and image based Q&A.

Tasks (implemented on Hi3403):

1. Deploy lightweight ASR (e.g., WeNet) for offline speech to text.

2. Deploy a compact VLM or vision model for scene understanding (e.g., lane detection, anomaly recognition).

3. Deploy a lightweight TTS (FastSpeech + LPCNet) for text to speech synthesis.

4. Integrate ASR → VLM/analysis → TTS into a complete conversational pipeline.

5. Optimize with INT8/INT4 quantization, operator fusion.

6. Demonstrate at least one use case (e.g., voice controlled navigation or sentry alert).

Expected targets:

1. Fully offline operation.

2. LLM generation speed ≥21 tokens/s.

3. End to end response time ≤5 seconds.

4. Deliver thesis, source code, and test report.

rows.themeProjectDescription:
1. Background: This project is focused on a hot topic issue: high-resolution direction finding technology based on sparse array in the field of array signal processing currently. Sparse arrays can overcome the main shortcomings of traditional uniform arrays, and improve the spatial resolution and direction-finding performance of array systems and reduce the system cost. Due to these advantages, sparse array direction-finding technology have broad application prospects in radar, communications, electronic reconnaissance and other fields. The research achievements of this project will establish the theoretical foundation for the applications of sparse array direction-finding technology in radar, communications, electronic reconnaissance and other fields.

2. Main task: Familiar with typical sparse array configurations such as nested arrays and coprime arrays; Mastering coarray output signal modeling; Research on high-resolution DOA estimation algorithm using sparse arrays.

3. Expected outcomes: research report, Matlab simulation code.

rows.themePrerequisiteSkills: Students are expected to have basic knowledge of navigation principles, signal processing, linear algebra, probability, and programming. Experience in MATLAB, Python, or C/C++ is preferred. Familiarity with GNSS/BeiDou positioning, inertial sensors, Kalman filtering, sensor fusion, and trajectory analysis would be highly beneficial. Basic understanding of drones, robotics, or intelligent transportation systems is desirable.
rows.themeProjectDescription:
1. Background

The BeiDou Navigation Satellite System has become a major enabling technology for positioning, navigation, timing, and intelligent applications in China and beyond. In recent years, low-altitude economy, intelligent transportation, unmanned systems, and infrastructure inspection have all created increasing demand for high-accuracy and high-reliability positioning solutions. In Hainan, this demand is particularly relevant due to the development of coastal transportation, island logistics, low-altitude UAV applications, and digital infrastructure management.

However, standalone BeiDou positioning performance may degrade in practical scenarios due to signal blockage, multipath, limited satellite visibility, atmospheric disturbances, and temporary interruptions. For intelligent inspection tasks using drones or mobile platforms, positioning continuity is as important as positioning accuracy. Integrating BeiDou with an inertial navigation system (INS) is a practical and widely adopted solution, where inertial sensing provides short-term continuity and GNSS provides long-term correction.

2. Main Task

This project aims to develop a BeiDou/INS integrated positioning method for low-altitude intelligent inspection applications. The student will first study the principles of BeiDou positioning, inertial sensor errors, coordinate systems, motion modeling, and data fusion algorithms. The project may use public GNSS/IMU datasets, simulation data, or small-scale experimental datadepending on resource availability.

The main technical work is to implement and evaluate a fusion algorithm based on Kalman Filter, Extended Kalman Filter, Unscented Kalman Filter, or equivalent sensor fusion schemes. The system should estimate position, velocity, and possibly attitude information, and compare the performance of standalone BeiDou, standalone INS dead reckoning, and integrated BeiDou/INS solutions. The student is encouraged to consider realistic scenarios such as partial signal blockage or short GNSS outages of 5–20 seconds.

Quantitative objectives may include reducing positioning error by at least 30% compared with standalone BeiDou under degraded signal conditions, maintaining continuous trajectory output during simulated outages, and achieving stable trajectory reconstruction in representative inspection scenarios.

3. Expected Outcomes

Expected outcomes include a BeiDou/INS positioning algorithm, a simulation or experimental evaluation platform, and a quantitative comparison of different positioning strategies. The final system should demonstrate improved accuracy, continuity, and robustness in low-altitude or mobile inspection scenarios. The dissertation should include theoretical modeling, algorithm implementation, trajectory analysis, and error statistics under multiple test conditions. This project is especially suitable for students interested in navigation, intelligent systems, low-altitude applications, and BeiDou-enabled engineering innovation.
rows.themeTitle: BeiDou/INS Integrated High-Precision Positioning for Low-Altitude Intelligent Inspection Applications
rows.themeUniversity: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

rows.themePrerequisiteSkills: Students should have a sound foundation in Signals and Systems, Digital Signal Processing, Communication Principles, and probability/statistics. Programming skills in MATLAB or Python are required. Familiarity with Fourier transform, time-frequency analysis, spectrogram generation, machine learning, and deep learning classification models will be beneficial. Basic knowledge of wireless communication or satellite navigation systems is preferred.
rows.themeProjectDescription:
1. Background

Communication and navigation systems increasingly operate in dense and complex electromagnetic environments, where different forms of intentional or unintentional interference may significantly degrade system reliability and service quality. In wireless communication systems, interference may reduce throughput and increase bit error rate; in navigation systems, especially satellite-based systems such as BeiDou, interference may cause signal loss, tracking failure, or severe positioning degradation. Therefore, accurate recognition of interference types is an important prerequisite for adaptive anti-jamming and interference mitigation.

Traditional interference recognition methods typically rely on manually designed features derived from the spectrum, energy distribution, bandwidth, or statistical properties of the received signal. These methods are often limited when dealing with low signal-to-noise ratio, mixed interference, or highly dynamic signal environments. By combining time-frequency analysis with deep learning, interference recognition can be formulated as a data-driven pattern classification problem, allowing automatic extraction of discriminative features from spectrogram-like representations.

2. Main Task

This project aims to investigate intelligent recognition of communication/navigation interference signals using time-frequency analysis and deep learning techniques. The student will first model or simulate several representative interference types, such as single-tone interference, multi-tone interference, narrowband interference, broadband noise interference, chirp interference, pulsed interference, and sweep interference. A dataset containing around 5,000–15,000 signal samples under different SNR or JSR conditions is recommended.

The student will then generate time-frequency representations using methods such as Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), wavelet transform, or other suitable approaches, and compare their effectiveness. Based on these representations, a classifier using CNN, ResNet, MobileNet, Vision Transformer, or a hybrid deep network will be designed and trained. The project should compare multiple architectures and evaluate robustness under different noise levels, especially under low-SNR conditions.

Quantitative research targets may include classification accuracy of above 90% under moderate conditions and above 80% under low-SNR scenarios, together with clear confusion matrix analysis and robustness evaluation.

3. Expected Outcomes

Expected outcomes include a simulated interference dataset, a complete time-frequency feature extraction and classification pipeline, and a trained deep learning model for interference recognition. The final report should demonstrate the ability of the proposed method to distinguish multiple interference categories with satisfactory robustness. Evaluation should include accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrix, and sensitivity to SNR/JSR variations. This topic is well aligned with the strengths of electronic information engineering, intelligent signal processing, and communication systems, and is particularly suitable for students considering postgraduate study in communications, signal processing, or navigation.
rows.themeTitle: Communication/Navigation Interference Signal Recognition Based on Time-Frequency Analysis and Deep Learning
rows.themeUniversity: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

rows.themePrerequisiteSkills: Students are expected to have a basic background in Python programming, digital image processing, machine learning, and deep learning. Familiarity with PyTorch/TensorFlow, OpenCV, and object detection or image segmentation methods is desirable. rows.themeProjectDescription:
1. Background

Roads and bridges are key components of modern transportation infrastructure, and their service safety is closely related to regular inspection and maintenance. Surface defects such as cracks, potholes, spalling, exposed reinforcement, and water seepage may gradually develop into serious structural problems if not identified at an early stage. Conventional manual inspection methods are often labor-intensive, subjective, slow, and difficult to scale, especially in large-area or hard-to-access scenarios. With recent advances in deep learning and computer vision, image-based automatic defect detection has become a highly promising approach for intelligent infrastructure inspection.

For Hainan and similar coastal or rapidly developing regions, the need for efficient transportation maintenance and digital infrastructure management is increasing. Therefore, a practical and lightweight AI-based detection system is of clear engineering relevance. Since deployment on mobile or edge devices is desirable in real applications, both detection accuracy and computational efficiency should be considered.

2. Main Task

This project aims to develop a lightweight deep learning framework for automatic detection and quantitative assessment of road and bridge surface defects. The student will first review common defect categories and prepare a labeled dataset using public data and/or self-collected images. A dataset of approximately 1,500–3,000 images covering at least 4–6 common defect typesis recommended. The project will then implement a baseline model using architectures such as YOLOv8, YOLOv10, RT-DETR, or lightweight segmentation networks, followed by optimization for small-target detection, robustness under illumination variation, and reduced model complexity.

Possible technical improvements include data augmentation, attention mechanisms, lightweight backbones, pruning, and feature fusion strategies. In addition to defect localization, the student is encouraged to explore basic quantitative indicators such as crack length, defect area, or severity level estimation. The target is to achieve mAP@0.5 above 80% , with an inference speed suitable for near real-time testing, e.g., above 15–20 FPS on a standard GPU platform.

3. Expected Outcomes

Expected outcomes include a defect image dataset, a trained lightweight detection model, a comparative evaluation against baseline methods, and a prototype interface for result visualization. The final system should be able to identify major surface defects and provide basic quantitative inspection outputs. The dissertation is expected to include model design, experimental validation, ablation studies, and performance comparison in terms of precision, recall, F1-score, mAP, inference speed, and model size. This project is suitable for students interested in AI, computer vision, and intelligent infrastructure applications.
rows.themeTitle: Lightweight Deep Learning-Based Detection and Quantitative Assessment of Road and Bridge Surface Defects
rows.themeUniversity: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

rows.themeProjectDescription:
Background: Camouflaged object detection (COD) aims to identify and locate objects that are visually similar to the surrounding environment. Compared with ordinary object detection or segmentation, COD is more difficult because camouflaged objects usually have weak boundaries, low contrast, confusing texture, and complex backgrounds. This project studies deep-learning-based COD methods. The main datasets used in this project are CAMO, COD10K, and NC4K, which will be used for data preprocessing, model training or testing, metric comparison, and visual result analysis.

Main tasks: 1.Understand the definition, application scenarios, research significance, and common evaluation metrics of camouflaged object detection; 2.Study basic deep learning detection or segmentation models and understand the workflow from image input to mask output; 3.Become familiar with PyTorch, including environment setup, data loading, model calling, training, inference, and result saving; 4.Preprocess CAMO, COD10K, and NC4K, including image-mask pairing, data organization, resizing, normalization, and dataset loader construction; 5.Improve a baseline COD model and record its performance under different metrics; 6.Compare testing metrics on CAMO, COD10K, and NC4K with tables, visualize detection masks and overlays, and analyze model advantages and limitations in simple scenes; 7.Develop a visualization interface for the complete COD workflow, including image input, model inference, camouflaged object mask generation, result overlay, metric display, and final output visualization.

Expected outcomes: The project is expected to complete a deep-learning-based camouflaged object detection system, achieve recognition and localization of camouflaged objects in simple scenes, conduct experiments and comparisons on CAMO, COD10K, and NC4K, provide visualized detection results and metric tables, develop a visualization demo for the full workflow, and complete the graduation thesis.

rows.themeProjectDescription:
Background:

UAV aerial images are widely used in smart transportation, urban monitoring, agriculture, emergency response, and remote sensing. Because UAV images are usually captured from high altitude and oblique viewpoints, the objects in the images are often small, densely distributed, partially occluded, and mixed with complex backgrounds. In this project, object detection clearly means recognizing and locating targets captured in UAV aerial images, such as vehicles, pedestrians, and other ground objects, rather than detecting the UAV itself. The main experimental dataset for this project is VisDrone2019, which will be used for model training, validation, testing, and comparison. YOLOv11 provides a strong one-stage detection framework with a good balance between accuracy and speed, making it suitable for object recognition and detection in UAV aerial images.


Main tasks:

1. Study the research status and development trend of object detection in UAV aerial images, especially small-object detection under complex backgrounds.

2. Analyze the basic architecture of YOLOv11, including its backbone, neck, detection head, feature extraction process, and inference workflow.

3. Build the experimental pipeline based on the VisDrone2019 dataset, including data preprocessing, annotation format conversion if needed, training configuration, validation, and testing.

4. Improve YOLOv11 according to the characteristics of UAV aerial images in VisDrone2019, focusing on small targets, dense targets, occlusion, scale changes, and complex scenes.

5. Design or optimize multi-scale feature fusion modules to improve the model's ability to detect objects of different sizes in UAV images.

6. Conduct experiments on VisDrone2019 and compare the improved method with YOLOv5, YOLOv7, the original YOLOv11, and other mainstream detection methods using metrics such as precision, recall, mAP, inference speed, parameter size, and computational cost.

7. Develop a visualization interface to demonstrate the complete workflow on UAV aerial images, including image upload or selection, YOLOv11 model inference, target box drawing, category recognition, confidence display, and final detection result output.


Expected outcomes:

The project is expected to improve YOLOv11 for recognizing and detecting targets in UAV aerial images, complete training and experimental comparison on the VisDrone2019 dataset, implement a visualization demo for the detection workflow, and write a graduation thesis explaining the model design, dataset processing, technical route, experiments, results, and conclusions.
rows.themeSourceRemarks: Object Detection in UAV Aerial Images Based on VisDrone2019
rows.themeTitle: Research on YOLOv11-Based Object Recognition and Detection in UAV Aerial Images

rows.themeProjectDescription:
Background:

Diffusion models have become an important class of generative models for image synthesis and image editing. Compared with traditional image processing methods, diffusion-based methods can follow text instructions, preserve visual realism, and support local or global modifications of image content. This project studies image editing methods based on diffusion models and focuses on understanding their principles, implementation workflow, evaluation methods, and practical prototype development.


Main tasks:

1. Understand the basic principles of generative diffusion models and their applications in image generation.

2. Master mainstream diffusion-model-based image editing methods, including text-guided editing, local editing, and global image modification.

3. Become familiar with mainstream deep learning frameworks and related diffusion model libraries.

4. Try to improve an existing image editing diffusion model, such as through prompt design, attention control, mask guidance, model component adjustment, or result post-processing.

5. Conduct comprehensive quantitative and qualitative analysis on benchmark datasets, and compare the proposed or improved method with existing advanced models.

6. Use methods such as attention map visualization to analyze how the model understands and associates text instructions with image regions, and explain the editing results.

7. Build a visualization interface to demonstrate the complete input-to-output workflow, including image input, text instruction input, editing process, and edited image output.


Expected outcomes:

The project is expected to design and implement a prototype system for image editing based on diffusion models. The system should modify local or global image content according to user-provided text instructions. The final outcomes include the prototype system, experimental comparison and analysis, visualization results, and a graduation thesis describing the design, implementation, experiments, and conclusions.

rows.themeTitle: Research and Implementation of Diffusion Model Based Image Editing Methods
